description: Rules for checking the skill end to end, one per feature that changes how a pcap must be built. Give the agent only the prompt. A run passes when every expectation holds.
common_expectations: The agent ran preflight before building and used Dalton (or asked before using the docker fallback).
The output directory holds the pcap, build.py, pcapkit.py, test.rules and README.md.
Running build.py twice gives a byte-identical pcap.
pcap_lint.py reports no errors, and any warnings are explained in the README.
dalton_client.py test passes: the sid fires on every engine that loads the rule; engines in not_loaded are reported as unsupported, not as failures.
The README lists what was invented and does not present invented details as researched.

evals.prompt: Build a pcap that fires this rule: alert dns any any -> any any (msg:"DNS lookup of suricata.io"; flow:to_server; dns.query; content:"suricata|2e|io"; bsize:11; sid:9100001; rev:1;)
expectations: The query name is exactly suricata.io (bsize 11), with a matching answer.

evals.prompt: Make me a pcap for: alert tcp $HOME_NET any -> $EXTERNAL_NET 6667 (msg:"IRC bot registers with sTorM nick"; flow:established,to_server; dsize:24; content:"NICK|20|sTorM|5b|"; offset:0; depth:11; nocase; content:"|5d 0d 0a|"; endswith; sid:9100002; rev:1;)
expectations: The NICK line is its own 24-byte segment.
The surrounding IRC registration (server notices, USER, JOIN) is plausible.

evals.prompt:
I need traffic that fires sid 9100004 here:
alert http $HOME_NET any -> $EXTERNAL_NET any (msg:"LinkedIn-themed request"; flow:established,to_server; http.method; content:"GET"; http.host; content:"linkedin.com"; flowbits:set,linkedin.req; flowbits:noalert; sid:9100003; rev:1;)
alert http $EXTERNAL_NET any -> $HOME_NET any (msg:"EXE served after LinkedIn-themed request"; flow:established,to_client; file.data; content:"MZ"; startswith; byte_jump:4,58,relative,little; content:"PE|00 00|"; distance:-64; within:4; flowbits:isset,linkedin.req; sid:9100004; rev:1;)
expectations: The request and the EXE response share one TCP connection (flowbits are per flow).
The EXE is inert (e.g. pcapkit.inert_pe), not a working binary.
The test expects only 9100004; 9100003 is noalert.

evals.prompt: Pcap please: alert http $EXTERNAL_NET any -> $HOME_NET any (msg:"Scripted account registration"; flow:established,to_server; http.method; content:"POST"; http.uri; content:"/api/register"; http.request_body; content:"email="; threshold:type both, track by_src, count 5, seconds 300; sid:9100005; rev:1;)
expectations: At least five qualifying POSTs from one source inside 300 seconds.
The test uses --set runmode=single; the README doesn't promise which packet the alert lands on in Dalton's default runmode.

evals.prompt: Build a pcap for: alert smtp $EXTERNAL_NET any -> $HOME_NET any (msg:"Mail from PayPal look-alike"; flow:established,to_server; smtp.mail_from; content:"@paypa1.com>"; nocase; endswith; sid:9100006; rev:1;)
expectations: A complete SMTP session (banner through QUIT).
The result and README say the rule needs Suricata 8 (smtp.mail_from) and list older engines as not loaded.

evals.prompt:
alert tcp $HOME_NET any -> $EXTERNAL_NET 8443 (msg:"317-byte opening message"; flow:established,to_server; dsize:317; stream_size:server,=,1; sid:9100007; rev:1;)
Can you make a pcap that triggers that?
expectations: The 317-byte client message is the first data on the connection, before the server sends anything.

evals.prompt: Generate a pcap that fires: alert tcp any any -> any any (msg:"Large length field in custom header"; flow:established,to_server; byte_test:2,>,40000,4; sid:9100008; rev:1;)
expectations: Bytes 4-5 of the matching payload, read big-endian, exceed 40000, as part of a coherent protocol header.

evals.prompt: Build a pcap for: alert tls $EXTERNAL_NET any -> any any (msg:"ZeroSSL-issued cert on TLS 1.2"; flow:established,from_server; tls.version:1.2; tls.cert_issuer; content:"ZeroSSL"; sid:9100009; rev:1;)
expectations: A real TLS 1.2 handshake whose server certificate issuer contains ZeroSSL.
The README says the certificate is self-minted and won't verify.

evals.prompt: Make a pcap for: alert http $EXTERNAL_NET any -> $HOME_NET any (msg:"Base64-wrapped DLL download"; flow:established,to_client; file_data; from_base64; content:"MZ"; depth:2; byte_jump:4,58,relative,little; content:"PE|00 00|"; distance:-64; within:4; sid:9100010; rev:1;)
expectations: The response body is base64 text of an inert PE.
The result notes the rule needs Suricata 8 (from_base64).
